title: Unification of Upper and Lower Egypt
description: King Narmer (Menes) unified Upper and Lower Egypt, founding the First Dynasty and one of history's earliest nation-states.

title: Great Pyramid of Giza built
description: Pharaoh Khufu completed the Great Pyramid, the largest of the Giza pyramids and the last surviving Wonder of the Ancient World.

title: Reign of Tutankhamun begins
description: The boy-king Tutankhamun took the throne, restoring traditional polytheism after Akhenaten's religious reforms.

title: Alexander the Great conquers Egypt
description: Alexander took Egypt from Persia and founded Alexandria, ushering in the Greek Ptolemaic dynasty.

title: Death of Cleopatra and Roman annexation
description: The death of Cleopatra VII ended Ptolemaic rule, and Egypt became a province of the Roman Empire.

title: Founding of Cairo by the Fatimids
description: The Fatimid dynasty founded Cairo as their capital and established al-Azhar, a center of Islamic learning.

title: Opening of the Suez Canal
description: The Suez Canal opened, linking the Mediterranean and Red Seas and transforming global maritime trade.

title: Egyptian Revolution and end of monarchy
description: The Free Officers Movement overthrew King Farouk, leading to a republic with Nasser later rising to power.

title: Portuguese reach Bioko island
description: Portuguese explorer Fernão do Pó sighted the island later named Fernando Pó (now Bioko), beginning European contact.

title: Spain acquires the territory
description: Under the Treaty of El Pardo, Portugal ceded the islands and mainland rights to Spain, forming Spanish Guinea.

title: Independence from Spain
description: Equatorial Guinea gained independence from Spain, with Francisco Macías Nguema becoming its first president.

title: Obiang seizes power in a coup
description: Teodoro Obiang Nguema overthrew his uncle Macías, beginning one of the world's longest-running presidencies.

title: Major offshore oil discoveries
description: Discovery of large offshore oil reserves transformed the economy, making the country a significant petroleum exporter.

title: Capital relocation project at Oyala
description: The government began building a planned new capital, later named Ciudad de la Paz, in the mainland interior.

title: Rise of the Kingdom of Aksum
description: The Aksumite kingdom flourished across present-day Eritrea and Ethiopia, controlling Red Sea trade through the port of Adulis.

title: Ottomans establish Habesh province
description: The Ottoman Empire seized the port of Massawa and coastal areas, ruling parts of the Eritrean coast for centuries.

title: Italy proclaims the colony of Eritrea
description: Italy consolidated its coastal holdings into the colony of Eritrea, with Asmara later becoming the capital.

title: Federation with Ethiopia
description: A UN resolution federated Eritrea with Ethiopia, which Ethiopia later dissolved by annexing the territory in 1962.

title: Start of the war of independence
description: The Eritrean armed struggle for independence began, lasting three decades against Ethiopian rule.

title: EPLF takes Asmara
description: The Eritrean People's Liberation Front captured Asmara, ending the long war and establishing de facto independence.

title: Independence after referendum
description: An overwhelming referendum vote led to formal independence, and Eritrea joined the United Nations.

title: Eritrean-Ethiopian War begins
description: A border dispute erupted into a deadly war with Ethiopia, lasting until a peace agreement in 2000.

title: Swazi nation consolidates under Ngwane III
description: Ngwane III led the Swazi people into the region, traditionally regarded as a founder of the Swazi kingdom.

title: Reign of King Mswati II
description: King Mswati II expanded the kingdom and strengthened the Swazi military, lending his name to the modern monarchy.

title: British protectorate established
description: Following the Boer War, Swaziland became a British protectorate administered as a high commission territory.

title: Independence under King Sobhuza II
description: Swaziland gained independence from Britain as a constitutional monarchy led by King Sobhuza II.

title: Sobhuza II suspends the constitution
description: The king repealed the independence constitution and banned political parties, consolidating royal power.

title: Coronation of King Mswati III
description: Mswati III was crowned king, becoming one of the world's last absolute monarchs.

title: Renamed the Kingdom of Eswatini
description: King Mswati III renamed the country Eswatini, meaning 'land of the Swazis,' on the 50th anniversary of independence.

title: Tradition of the Solomonic dynasty's origins
description: Ethiopian tradition traces the imperial line to Menelik I, son of King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba.

title: Kingdom of Aksum at its height
description: Aksum became a major trading empire minting its own coinage and ranked among the great powers of the ancient world.

title: Aksum adopts Christianity
description: King Ezana converted to Christianity, making Aksum one of the earliest Christian states in the world.

title: Rise of the Zagwe dynasty
description: The Zagwe dynasty came to power and later built the famous rock-hewn churches of Lalibela.

title: Restoration of the Solomonic dynasty
description: Yekuno Amlak overthrew the Zagwe and restored the Solomonic line, which ruled Ethiopia for centuries.

title: Battle of Adwa
description: Emperor Menelik II's forces decisively defeated Italy, securing Ethiopia's independence and inspiring anti-colonial movements.

title: Italian occupation under Mussolini
description: Fascist Italy invaded and briefly occupied Ethiopia, forcing Emperor Haile Selassie into exile until 1941.

title: Fall of Haile Selassie and the Derg
description: A Marxist military junta, the Derg, deposed Emperor Haile Selassie, ending centuries of monarchy.

title: Portuguese explorers reach the coast
description: Portuguese navigators reached the Gabon estuary, naming the region after the Portuguese word 'gabão' for a cloak.

title: France establishes a foothold
description: France signed treaties with coastal Mpongwe chiefs, beginning its colonial presence on the Gabon estuary.

title: Founding of Libreville
description: Freed slaves settled the site that became Libreville, 'free town,' the future capital of Gabon.

title: Albert Schweitzer founds Lambaréné hospital
description: Physician Albert Schweitzer established his renowned hospital at Lambaréné, later earning him the Nobel Peace Prize.

title: Independence from France
description: Gabon gained independence from France, with Léon M'ba becoming its first president.

title: Omar Bongo becomes president
description: Omar Bongo took power and ruled Gabon for over four decades, presiding over an oil-driven economy.

title: Creation of 13 national parks
description: Gabon established a network of national parks covering about 11% of its territory to protect rainforest wildlife.

title: Portuguese explore the Gambia River
description: Portuguese navigators explored the Gambia River, opening the region to European trade.

title: Early European trading settlements
description: Courland and later English traders established posts along the river to trade in gold, ivory, and enslaved people.

title: Founding of Bathurst (Banjul)
description: The British established Bathurst, now Banjul, as a trading base and post to suppress the slave trade.

title: Independence from Britain
description: The Gambia gained independence from the United Kingdom, with Dawda Jawara as its first leader.

title: The Gambia becomes a republic
description: The Gambia became a republic within the Commonwealth, with Dawda Jawara as its first president.

title: Jammeh seizes power in a coup
description: Yahya Jammeh led a military coup, beginning a 22-year authoritarian rule over the country.

title: Democratic transition to Adama Barrow
description: After losing elections, Jammeh left power under regional pressure, allowing Adama Barrow to take office.

title: Akan states and gold trade flourish
description: Akan peoples developed states across the forest region, trading gold along trans-Saharan routes.

title: Portuguese build Elmina Castle
description: The Portuguese constructed Elmina Castle, the first European fort in sub-Saharan Africa, on the Gold Coast.

title: Rise of the Ashanti Empire
description: Osei Tutu unified Akan states into the powerful Ashanti Empire, symbolized by the Golden Stool.

title: Britain forms the Gold Coast colony
description: After wars with the Ashanti, Britain established the Gold Coast as a crown colony.

title: First sub-Saharan colony to gain independence
description: Led by Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African nation to win independence from colonial rule.

title: Coup overthrows Nkrumah
description: A military and police coup ousted President Kwame Nkrumah while he was abroad, ending his rule.

title: Return to multiparty democracy
description: Ghana adopted a new constitution and held multiparty elections, establishing a stable democratic system.

title: Region within the Mali Empire
description: Much of present-day Guinea fell under the Mali Empire founded by Sundiata Keita, a hub of gold and trade.

title: Imamate of Futa Jallon established
description: Fulani Muslims founded a theocratic state in the Futa Jallon highlands, a major center of Islamic scholarship.

title: Capture of Samori Touré
description: French forces captured the resistance leader Samori Touré, completing colonial conquest of the region.

title: Independence by rejecting French Community
description: Guinea voted 'No' in a referendum and became independent under Ahmed Sékou Touré, the only colony to do so immediately.

title: Military takes power after Sékou Touré's death
description: Following the death of Sékou Touré, the military seized power with Lansana Conté becoming president.

title: First free presidential election
description: Guinea held its first democratic presidential election, won by Alpha Condé after decades of authoritarian rule.

title: Ebola epidemic begins in Guinea
description: The deadliest Ebola outbreak in history was first detected in southeastern Guinea before spreading across West Africa.

title: Portuguese reach the coast
description: Portuguese navigators reached the rivers and coast of present-day Guinea-Bissau, beginning European trade contacts.

title: Cacheu becomes a trading hub
description: The Portuguese established Cacheu as a major slave-trading port on the Upper Guinea coast.

title: Portuguese Guinea formed as a colony
description: Portugal separated the territory from Cape Verde, establishing Portuguese Guinea as a distinct colony.

title: Amílcar Cabral founds the PAIGC
description: Amílcar Cabral co-founded the PAIGC, which led the armed struggle for independence from Portugal.

title: Unilateral declaration of independence
description: The PAIGC declared independence after a long liberation war; Portugal recognized it in 1974.

title: Coup led by João Bernardo Vieira
description: A military coup brought João Bernardo Vieira to power, beginning decades of political instability.

title: Civil war erupts
description: A brief but devastating civil war broke out between government forces and a military junta.

title: First French missionaries arrive
description: French missionaries landed on the coast, marking early European contact with the region.

title: France establishes coastal protectorates
description: France signed treaties with coastal kings, building forts and beginning its colonial presence.

title: Ivory Coast becomes a French colony
description: France formally declared Côte d'Ivoire a colony within French West Africa.

title: Independence under Houphouët-Boigny
description: Côte d'Ivoire gained independence from France, with Félix Houphouët-Boigny as its first president.

title: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace completed
description: The vast Basilica of Our Lady of Peace was completed in Yamoussoukro, among the largest churches in the world.

title: Civil war divides the country
description: A failed coup sparked a civil war that split Côte d'Ivoire between a rebel-held north and government-held south.

title: Post-election crisis ends
description: A violent crisis following disputed 2010 elections ended with Alassane Ouattara taking office.

title: Early human settlement around Lake Turkana
description: The Lake Turkana region preserves some of the earliest evidence of human ancestors and prehistoric life.

title: Rise of Swahili coastal city-states
description: Trading cities like Mombasa and Malindi flourished along the coast, blending African, Arab, and Persian cultures.

title: Vasco da Gama reaches the coast
description: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama landed at Malindi and Mombasa en route to India.

title: British East Africa Protectorate
description: Britain established the East Africa Protectorate, later building the Uganda Railway through Kenya.

title: Mau Mau uprising begins
description: The Mau Mau rebellion against British colonial rule erupted, prompting a state of emergency and violent suppression.

title: Independence under Jomo Kenyatta
description: Kenya gained independence from Britain, with Jomo Kenyatta becoming its first prime minister and later president.

title: Wangari Maathai wins Nobel Peace Prize
description: Environmentalist Wangari Maathai became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

title: New constitution adopted
description: Kenyans approved a new constitution introducing devolved county government and a bill of rights.

title: Moshoeshoe I founds the Basotho nation
description: King Moshoeshoe I united Sotho-speaking peoples at Thaba Bosiu during the upheavals of the Mfecane.

title: Free State-Basotho War
description: Conflict erupted between the Basotho and Boer settlers of the Orange Free State over land.

title: British protectorate of Basutoland
description: Moshoeshoe sought British protection, and Basutoland became a protectorate to avoid Boer annexation.

title: Independence as the Kingdom of Lesotho
description: Basutoland gained independence from Britain as the Kingdom of Lesotho under King Moshoeshoe II.

title: Military coup
description: A military coup overthrew the government of Leabua Jonathan, beginning a period of army rule.

title: Election unrest and regional intervention
description: Disputed elections triggered unrest, prompting a military intervention by South Africa and Botswana.

title: Lesotho Highlands Water Project phase opens
description: Major dams of the Lesotho Highlands Water Project exported water to South Africa, a key economic resource.

title: American Colonization Society settles freed slaves
description: The American Colonization Society established a settlement of freed African Americans at Cape Mesurado.

title: Liberia declares independence
description: Liberia declared itself an independent republic, becoming Africa's first independent republic.

title: Firestone rubber concession
description: Firestone established a vast rubber plantation, making rubber central to Liberia's economy for decades.

title: Samuel Doe seizes power in a coup
description: Master Sergeant Samuel Doe led a coup that ended over a century of Americo-Liberian political dominance.

title: First Liberian Civil War begins
description: Charles Taylor's rebellion launched a brutal civil war that devastated the country for years.

title: End of the Second Civil War
description: A peace agreement ended Liberia's civil wars and led to Charles Taylor's exile and a transitional government.

title: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf inaugurated
description: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf became Africa's first elected female head of state and later won the Nobel Peace Prize.
